topic: Privacy, compliance and chain economics for a fully on-chain NFT protocol (RAILGUN, stealth addresses ERC-5564/6538, Privacy Pools, OFAC/Tornado lessons, messaging legality, 2026 SSTORE2 cost tables, L2 fees after blobs, Pectra/Fusaka/Glamsterdam, DA choices, target-chain recommendation)
method_note: Live reads of OP-stack GasPriceOracle / Arbitrum ArbGasInfo via the Blockscout connector were denied by the session permission layer; L2 L1-data-fee figures are computed from the published Fjord formula with illustrative scalars and flagged as such.

findings.claim: ERC-5564 (Final) announcer singleton is 0x55649E01B5Df198D18D95b5cc5051630cfD45564; announce(uint256 schemeId,address stealthAddress,bytes ephemeralPubKey,bytes metadata); scheme 1 = secp256k1 with view tags.
findings.relevance: Cheapest privacy feature for the token's vault; identical address on every target chain.

findings.claim: ERC-6538 (Final) registry singleton is 0x6538E6bf4B0eBd30A8Ea093027Ac2422ce5d6538; registerKeysOnBehalf accepts EIP-712 or EIP-1271 signatures, so a contract account (ERC-6551) can register a stealth meta-address.
findings.relevance: Lets each token's account be stealth-addressable.

findings.claim: Umbra processed >350,000 transactions and about $500M since May 2021 across Ethereum, Polygon, Optimism, Base, Arbitrum; v2 ~90% complete, summer-2026 target.
findings.relevance: Adoption evidence for stealth addresses (2026-02-18).

findings.claim: RAILGUN: Groth16/BN254 UTXO notes; shield()/transact() on RailgunSmartWallet; owner-settable shield/unshield fees capped at 50%; Ethereum proxy 0xfa7093cdd9ee6932b4eb2c9e1cde7ce00b1fa4b9 (same on Arbitrum); L2BEAT TVL $110.8M, 7-day governance upgrade delay, Base deployment initialized via governance.
findings.relevance: Candidate shielded rail; note upgradeability and trusted setup risks.

findings.claim: RAILGUN Private Proofs of Innocence use blocklists from Elliptic, ScamSniffer, PureFi, SlowMist and Chainalysis Sanctions Oracle; broadcasters require a valid PPOI; new shields have a 1-hour unshield-only standby period.
findings.relevance: Model for opt-in, non-custodial compliance.

findings.claim: A June 2026 measurement paper links 17.65% of RAILGUN withdrawals uniquely to deposits via timing, address reuse, graph proximity, amount fingerprints and knapsack sums; median anonymity loss 3.42 bits.
findings.relevance: UI defaults (round amounts, delays) matter more than cryptography.

findings.claim: Privacy Pools mainnet Entrypoint 0x6818809EefCe719E480a7526D76bD3e561526b46 and ETH pool 0xF241d57C6DebAe225c0F2e6eA1529373C9A9C9fB; interface: deposit(uint256 precommitment) payable, relay(Withdrawal,WithdrawProof,scope), updateRoot(root,ipfsCID), ragequit(RagequitProof) bypasses the ASP for the original depositor; Entrypoint is an upgradeable proxy.
findings.relevance: Shielded rail with a trustless exit; integrate via adapter.

findings.claim: Privacy Pools launched on Ethereum mainnet 31 March 2025 and reported ~$6M volume / >1,500 users by its Nov 2025 $3.5M seed round; integrated into the EF's Kohaku wallet.
findings.relevance: Scale of the compliant-privacy market (secondary press).

findings.claim: Fifth Circuit, Van Loon v. Treasury (No. 23-50669, 26 Nov 2024): Tornado Cash's immutable smart contracts are not 'property' under IEEPA because they are not capable of being owned; OFAC exceeded its authority; reversed and remanded.
findings.relevance: Immutability and absence of control are the legal shield; never add admin keys.

findings.claim: Treasury delisted Tornado Cash on 21 March 2025 citing novel legal and policy issues and its Van Loon filing, while warning about DPRK-linked transactions.
findings.relevance: Sanctions exposure of immutable code has receded; operator exposure has not.

findings.claim: FinCEN 2019 guidance: 'An anonymizing software provider is not a money transmitter'; an anonymizing services provider (mixer operator) is.
findings.relevance: Software vs service is the line our design must stay on.

findings.claim: Samourai Wallet founders pleaded guilty 30 Jul 2025 to conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money transmitting business; sentenced to 5 and 4 years (6 and 19 Nov 2025); forfeited $6.3M in fees.
findings.relevance: Operating infrastructure plus fees plus knowledge is prosecutable even for non-custodial software.

findings.claim: Roman Storm was convicted 6 Aug 2025 of conspiracy to operate an unlicensed money transmitting business (jury hung on laundering and sanctions counts); acquittal motion argued 9 Apr 2026 and still pending; retrial adjourned from 26 Oct 2026 to 26 Apr 2027.
findings.relevance: Developer liability remains unsettled (secondary press; DEF timeline primary through May 2025).

findings.claim: DOJ's 7 Apr 2025 'Ending Regulation by Prosecution' memo says DOJ will no longer target mixing services or offline wallets for acts of their end users except within stated priorities; NCET disbanded.
findings.relevance: Policy climate; summarised from law-firm notes, memo text not read directly.

findings.claim: CLARITY Act (with the Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act safe harbour for non-custodial developers in s.604) failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on 15 Sep 2026; not law.
findings.relevance: No statutory safe harbour exists; design must stand on its own (secondary tracker).

findings.claim: EU AMLR (Regulation 2024/1624) Article 79 bars CASPs from anonymous accounts and anonymity-enhancing coins from 1 July 2027.
findings.relevance: Launchpad tokens must not embed anonymity features (secondary summaries of the regulation).

findings.claim: EIP-7702 (Final): tx type 0x04; delegation designator 0xef0100||address; EXTCODESIZE of a delegated EOA returns 23; PER_AUTH_BASE_COST 12,500; security section warns of malicious delegates and front-run initialisation.
findings.relevance: Holder-verification logic must not use code.length==0 as an EOA test.

findings.claim: Wintermute (30 May 2025): over 97% of EIP-7702 delegations pointed to identical copy-pasted sweeper contracts draining compromised EOAs.
findings.relevance: Warn visitors whose EOA is delegated to known sweeper code.

findings.claim: Mainnet gas: 0.15 gwei standard (5 May 2026), 0.5 gwei April daily average; gas limit 60M; tx cap ~16.78M; rollups carry ~95% of transactions.
findings.relevance: L1 one-time writes are now cheap; per-action costs still favour L2.

findings.claim: EIP-7825 (Fusaka, mainnet 3 Dec 2025) caps any transaction at 16,777,216 gas; EIP-7607 lists Fusaka's EIPs and activation epoch 411392.
findings.relevance: Max three 24KB SSTORE2 chunks per transaction today.

findings.claim: Glamsterdam's scheduled list (EIP-7773) includes EIP-8037 (code deposit 200 -> 1,530 gas/byte), EIP-7954 (64 KiB code), EIP-8038, EIP-7976, EIP-2780, EIP-7708, EIP-7928, EIP-7997; Sepolia activation 6 Oct 2026; mainnet undecided.
findings.relevance: Post-8037 a 24KB chunk costs ~38M gas and no longer fits the 7825 cap; deploy L1 static assets before Glamsterdam.

findings.claim: EIP-8037 (Review): CPSB = 1,530 gas per state byte; code deposit 1,530 gas/byte; SSTORE 0->nonzero 97,920; new account 183,600; targets 120 GiB/yr state growth at 150M gas blocks.
findings.relevance: 7.65x increase in SSTORE2 write cost if adopted.

findings.claim: SSTORE2 cost today: 50 KB = 11.23M gas (~$15 at 0.5 gwei, ETH $2,750), 150 KB = 33.6M (~$46), 300 KB = 67.1M (~$92); on Base at 0.005 gwei ~$0.15/$0.46/$0.92 plus cents of L1 data fee; Arbitrum at 0.02 gwei ~$0.62/$1.85/$3.69; OP at 0.001 gwei ~$0.03/$0.09/$0.18.
findings.relevance: Computed from the gas schedule (model in scratchpad/sstore2_cost.py); prices from ethereum.org and Base docs.

findings.claim: OP Stack Fjord L1 data fee: l1Cost = estimatedSize(FastLZ) * (baseFeeScalar*l1BaseFee*16 + blobBaseFeeScalar*blobBaseFee) / 1e12; operator fee post-Jovian; Base minimum base fee 0.005 gwei, elasticity 6, denominator 125.
findings.relevance: L1 data component for Base deployments is negligible at 2026 blob prices.

findings.claim: Arbitrum prices L1 data by Brotli-compressed size * 16 at a dynamic L1 price per unit, converted to L2 gas; floor via ArbGasInfo.getMinimumGasPrice; trackers show ~0.02 gwei in late Sep 2026.
findings.relevance: Arbitrum is ~4x Base for execution-heavy writes today.

findings.claim: Blob target/max rose 6/9 -> 10/15 (BPO1, 9 Dec 2025) -> 14/21 (BPO2, 7 Jan 2026); EIP-7918 sets BLOB_BASE_COST 2^13 so blob gas is bounded below by ~base_fee/16; blobs are 4096x32 bytes, pruned after 4096 epochs (~18 days) and not EVM-readable.
findings.relevance: Blobs/alt-DA cannot serve a website from chain; only code in state can.

findings.claim: Measured L2 fees 15 Sep 2026 (ETH $2,475): transfer/swap Ethereum 0.336c/2.25c, Base 0.0314c/0.209c, Arbitrum 0.105c/0.697c, OP Mainnet 0.00543c/0.0353c.
findings.relevance: Per-action cost comparison (third-party measurement, oracle-priced).

findings.claim: EIP-4444 partial history expiry: all execution clients may drop pre-merge bodies/receipts since 1 May 2025; a rolling-window phase is planned for 2026 with timing unset.
findings.relevance: Log-only messaging history will need state-resident heads/ring buffers.

findings.claim: XMTP uses MLS (MLS_128_HPKEX25519_CHACHA20POLY1305_SHA256_Ed25519) with X-Wing KEM, forward secrecy and post-compromise security; nodes see only timing/size.
findings.relevance: Reference for what on-chain messaging gives up (PCS, deletion) versus permanence.

findings.claim: EU Council dropped mandatory client-side scanning from the CSA Regulation position on 26 Nov 2025 (trilogue continuing); UK accredited-technology notices exist but no accredited technology does; Apple withdrew ADP from new UK accounts in early 2025 after a TCN.
findings.relevance: Encryption remains lawful; only operators can be served notices, so operate nothing.

findings.claim: Umbra put its hosted front end into maintenance mode on 21 Apr 2026 after ~$800K of Kelp DAO exploit proceeds (18 Apr 2026, ~$292M) passed through it; contracts remained live.
findings.relevance: A front end is the only lever a non-custodial team has; a web3:// site has none.

findings.claim: Hegota (post-Glamsterdam, ~2027) currently schedules only EIP-7805 FOCIL and EIP-8141 Frame Transactions.
findings.relevance: Censorship resistance and alternative signature schemes are coming at L1 (secondary).

recommendations.recommendation: Ethereum mainnet is the canonical home (ERC-721, ERC-6551 accounts, vault, stealth registrations, immutable chain/band registry); Base is the high-frequency surface (mint waves, per-token AMM, launchpad, messaging).
recommendations.rationale: ethereum.org 2026 guidance favours L1 for neutrality and high-value state; privacy singletons and both compliant pools are mainnet-first; Van Loon rewards immutability; at 0.5 gwei a 300 KB engine costs ~$92 on L1, while a 200K-gas action costs ~$0.003 on Base.

recommendations.recommendation: Reduce id bands to Ethereum + Base (+ optionally OP Mainnet); drop Arbitrum and other chains from the band plan.
recommendations.rationale: OP Stack chains share fee code, predeploys and EIP cadence; Arbitrum's floor is ~4x Base's and its fee machinery differs; fewer bands halves deployment/verification surface.

recommendations.recommendation: Deploy all L1 static bytes before Glamsterdam mainnet and make the deployer gas-schedule-aware (block.gaslimit, EIP-7825 cap, fork benchmark, refuse chunks that will not fit).
recommendations.rationale: EIP-8037 as drafted raises code deposit to 1,530 gas/byte: 300 KB goes from 67M to 476M gas and a 24 KB chunk (38M gas) no longer fits the 16.78M per-tx cap.

recommendations.recommendation: No admin keys, no fees and no operator-run relayer or front end on any privacy or messaging path; fees only on market/launchpad.
recommendations.rationale: This is the line between Van Loon / FinCEN 4.5.1(b) (software, not property, not money transmission) and Samourai / Storm (operated service with fees).

recommendations.recommendation: Ship stealth receive first: each token's ERC-6551 account registers an ERC-6538 meta-address via registerKeysOnBehalf (ERC-1271); the site announces payments through the ERC-5564 singleton.
recommendations.rationale: One event per payment, deterministic singleton addresses on every chain, Final standards, 350K+ Umbra transactions of precedent.

recommendations.recommendation: Integrate Privacy Pools (mainnet, ragequit exit) and RAILGUN (where a Base deployment is confirmed) as adapters called from the vault; surface PPOI/ASP status; never fork a mixer.
recommendations.rationale: Both are live, audited-by-reputation rails with opt-in compliance; a fork would make us the operator.

recommendations.recommendation: Messaging: text-only, size-capped, log-based, optional E2EE using the ERC-6538 viewing key; keep the thread head and last N messages in state.
recommendations.rationale: Mitigates immutable-illegal-content exposure and survives EIP-4444 history expiry without an indexer.

recommendations.recommendation: Treat every connected account as a possible contract (ERC-1271 for any code, including 7702 designators); never request 7702 authorizations; use ERC-5792 batching; session keys never sign 1271; client warns on known sweeper code hashes.
recommendations.rationale: EXTCODESIZE of a delegated EOA is 23; >97% of early 7702 delegations were sweepers.

recommendations.recommendation: Launchpad-created tokens carry no anonymity features; privacy lives in the holder's account.
recommendations.rationale: EU AMLR Art. 79 makes anonymity-enhancing assets unlistable for CASPs from 1 Jul 2027.

recommendations.recommendation: Prefer EIP-7951 secp256r1 passkey session keys and plan for EIP-7708 transfer logs and EIP-7997 deterministic factory.
recommendations.rationale: Fusaka shipped the precompile; Glamsterdam schedules the other two; they simplify login, vault accounting and same-address deployment.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not build a mixer, relayer network, hosted front end or fee-taking privacy router; do not route through Tornado Cash despite delisting.
recommendations.rationale: Operator liability (Samourai, Storm retrial pending Apr 2027) and no statutory safe harbour (CLARITY failed cloture 15 Sep 2026).

special_ideas: Stealth-receivable agent: the token's ERC-6551 account publishes an ERC-6538 meta-address; anyone pays it privately via the ERC-5564 singleton; the site sweeps one-time addresses into the vault.
Clean-bill attestation slot: holder may post the hash of a PPOI proof or ASP membership root to the token; verifiable, optional, never enforced.
Ragequit-grade vault invariant: every shielded/pooled path has a public, permissionless exit, tested like Privacy Pools' ragequit.
Gas-regime-aware deployer: reads block.gaslimit, assumes the EIP-7825 cap, benchmarks a chunk on a fork, prints all-in USD per chain, refuses post-8037 chunks that cannot fit.
Dual-band canonicality: ownership on mainnet, surface on Base; the web3:// site on either chain resolves ownership against the L1 token.
Messages that survive history expiry: per-thread ring buffer in state plus log history; no indexer ever, no blank site after pruning.
Viewing-key messaging: the ERC-6538 viewing key doubles as the recipient key for encrypted messages, one registration for stealth receive and private DMs.
Passkey sessions via EIP-7951 secp256r1 bounded by existing session-key rules (expiry, spend cap, allowlists).
EIP-7708-ready vault: inbound ETH enumerable from logs post-Glamsterdam, balance-delta before.
One-address-per-app by construction: CREATE2 per-app sub-accounts under the token's account so swap, launchpad and messaging are unlinkable across apps.

Is RAILGUN live on Base and at what proxy address? L2BEAT says governance-initialized; RAILGUN docs list no Base address.
Will Privacy Pools deploy on Base? Currently Ethereum-only.
Outcome of Roman Storm's pending acquittal motion and the 26 Apr 2027 retrial.
Will the CLARITY Act's non-custodial developer safe harbour be revived after the failed 15 Sep 2026 cloture vote?
